disclaimer: All revenue, funding, debt, GPU-count, contract and risk figures are compiled from public company announcements, SEC/press filings and press reporting. They are best-effort estimates for visualization and education, NOT investment advice or authoritative financial data. Figures move fast in this sector -- verify against primary sources (10-K/6-K filings, company IR pages) before relying on them. Site coordinates are metro/campus-level approximations.

risk_methodology.name: Neocloud Risk Score

factor_definitions.customer_concentration: Share of revenue/backlog tied to one or two anchor customers. A single customer walking away (or renegotiating) can gut the business.
factor_definitions.leverage: Reliance on debt / SPV / vendor-financing structures (incl. circular vendor financing where a chip supplier is simultaneously investor, lender and customer) rather than equity to fund GPU and data-center capex.
factor_definitions.contract_mismatch: Gap between the tenor of debt/financing backing the GPUs and the tenor of the revenue contracts covering them. Short contracts stacked on long-dated debt = refinancing risk; long contracts that lock in one chip generation = obsolescence lock-in risk. For pure data-center landlords (no GPU ownership), this instead reflects lease structure -- long triple-net-style leases transfer the GPU refresh risk entirely to the GPU-owning tenant.
factor_definitions.chip_freshness: How exposed the fleet is to obsolescence. Majority-Hopper (H100/H200) or older AMD fleets score higher risk than fleets already on Blackwell/GB200-300/MI350-class silicon -- the crux of the Burry-style 'GPUs depreciate over 2-3 years, not 5-6' debate.

risk_methodology.note: Every company scored is a GPU neocloud (owns the GPUs). The score is model-agnostic: whether a neocloud owns its data centers or leases colocation, chip_freshness still reflects its own fleet's obsolescence exposure. The separate 'data-center owner' field names who owns the building/power at each site.

financing_graph.note: Directed edges src -> dst. This is the 'circular financing' web the sector is debated over: chip vendors invest in the neoclouds that buy their chips and in some cases lease compute back, while private credit funds the GPU purchases against the same GPUs as collateral.
